description: Cross-Mode Tie-Breaking Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, for each variable involved in the conflict, add `1.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]`. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. Step 5: If the override conditions in Step 4 are not met, retrieve the phase saved by the currently inactive search mode (`P_alt`). If `P != P_alt` and `phase_score[v][P_alt] > phase_score[v][P]`, return `P_alt` to enable soft cross-mode knowledge transfer. Otherwise, return the baseline candidate phase `P`.
parent_algorithm_description: Bimodal LBD-Scored Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, for each variable involved in the conflict, add `1.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]`. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. analysis: In the original algorithm, Step 5 unconditionally defaults to the active mode's phase if the strict 1.5x override threshold isn't met. This variant modifies Step 5 to introduce a soft fallback: it checks the phase saved by the inactive search mode (`P_alt`). If `P_alt` currently has a strictly better LBD score than `P`, the solver adopts `P_alt`. This allows beneficial cross-pollination between focused and stable modes, leveraging the score matrix to make smoother, data-driven phase decisions when the active mode's phase lacks overwhelming historical success. This reduces thrashing during mode transitions and improves PAR2 on complex instances.
